title: Money Planner Bundle: Sinking Funds, Emergency Fund, 50/30/20 Budget (Excel, Google Sheets)
description:
It splits this month's savings across your sinking funds and emergency fund, and tells you when one comes up short. Plus a paycheck plan that shows which payday pays which bill. For Excel and Google Sheets.

Money Steps Planner: every dollar gets a next step
• This month's money moves: your goal money split for you, emergency fund first, then every sinking fund in your order
• 5 money steps that tick themselves: every dollar has a job, starter cushion, funds on track, one month covered, full cushion
• Sinking funds: up to 20, each says what to move this month to be ready by its due date (no date = a yearly cost)
• Emergency ladder: starter cushion to 6 months, with the month you reach each rung at your pace
• Split: 50/30/20 or your own targets, with the biggest want to trim when you're over
• No-spend month: tap ✓ or Spent; a ✓ after a spending day counts as a comeback, no streaks to break
• 30-day wishlist: wishes wait first, then fit your wishlist money or get a small monthly amount
• Do this next: 4 plain-English steps written from your own numbers

Paycheque Plan, International edition: which payday covers which bill
• Left to spend until your next payday, bills placed on the right paycheque, a warning before a short payday
• Paste in your bank's CSV export; works with weekly, every-2-weeks, twice-a-month, monthly or every-4-weeks pay

Both planners:
• Ask AI: prompts built from your totals (never names) for the AI chat app you already use
• Reminders: your key dates, ready to import into Google Calendar
• Any currency: $, €, £, ₹ or your own symbol

What's in the download:
• Money Steps Planner: 8 spreadsheets (4 themes, Sample + Blank) and a 2-page quick-start PDF
• Paycheque Plan: 8 spreadsheets (4 themes, Sample + Blank) and a quick-start PDF
• Free updates: the Move My Data tab brings your entries into new versions in about 2 minutes

Good to know:
• Works in Microsoft 365, Excel 2019 or newer and Google Sheets
• No bank login: you type your numbers and the plan does the math
• The files don't use AI themselves; the prompts work with the AI tools you already have
• Money Steps Planner 1.0 was tested with 1,088 automated checks before release
• Digital download, nothing ships
• Best set up on a computer; ticking days and adding wishes works in the phone apps
• Launch price until Mon Nov 30, then $24

A planning tool for general education. It doesn't move money.

From Fully Funded, a Steadfold studio.
General education only, not financial advice.
